title: On the time a diffusion process spends along a line
summary: For an arbitrary diffusion process $X$ with time-homogeneous drift and variance parameters $μ(x)$ and $σ^2(x)$, let $V_\varepsilon$ be $1/\varepsilon$ times the total time $X(t)$ spends in the strip $[a+bt-(1/2)\varepsilon,a+bt+(1/2)\varepsilon]$.The limit $V$ as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0$ is the full halfline version of the local time of $X(t)-a-bt$ at zero, and can be thought of as the time $X$ spends along the straight line $x=a+bt$. We prove that $V$ is either infinite with probability 1 or distributed as a mixture of an exponential and a unit point mass at zero, and we give formulae for…
